newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Formosa mulls selling petrochemicals in China.
newsitem.headline: Formosa mulls selling petrochemicals in China.

text.p: Taiwan's Formosa Plastics group said on Wednesday it would consider selling some of its petrochemical products in China after completion of its oil refinery and petrochemical complex in Taiwan.
State-funded Central News Agency quoted Formosa chairman Wang Yung-ching as saying Formosa would consider shipping the petrochemical products to China for reprocessing and selling them there.

Wang made the comments during a meeting with a visiting business delegation from China's coastal Xiamen province, the agency said. He said the lack of proper distribution channels and heavy business and sales taxes would be the main concerns for the firm's possible business on the mainland.

Formosa group began construction of Taiwan's first private naphtha cracker in 1993. The US$9 billion oil refinery and petrochemical complex is expected to be complete by 1999, with the cracker aiming to start operations in 1998.
State oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum was also evaluating plans to build a US$5.5-$7.2 billion refinery and petrochemical complex, but said the project hinged on access to China's market.
Chinese Petroleum officials have said Taiwan must ease its ban on petroleum and petrochemical products' shipping links with China before the new project can become feasible.
Taiwan now only allows container ships to make limited direct crossings of the Taiwan strait, but still forbids direct cargo exchanges.
Containers arriving from the mainland cannot enter Taiwan customs and must be transshipped to other destinations.
